items.title: In Biochemistry
items.text:
• In biochemistry, particular reagent kits follow certain mathematical equations.

  • To use this kit, we need to calibrate it using the given controls. After calibration, a curve is generated, and tests may then be performed, with test results determined according to this curve.

  • Here you may see 5 data points that represent the controls. One should already know the control values.

While determining each control value, you may use the optimization method (see Finding Combinations) to determine the correct or approximate control values.

  • Plot

items.title: Measurement of Height Using a Sensor Module
items.text:
• When measuring distance using a sensor, the output signal is relatively small and its range differs from the MCU's ADC requirements. Therefore, an amplifier must be placed between them to adjust the signal range before feeding it into the MCU.
  • Once you receive the numerical sensor output from the MCU, you can perform mathematical operations on the data to generate graphs for acceleration, velocity, and distance.

items.title: μA741 🆕
items.text:
The μA741 operational amplifier was designed by Dave Fullagar in 1968 while working at Fairchild Semiconductor.

Note

Model parameters

  • Current gain: \( \beta = 200 \)
  • Forward Early voltage: \( V_{AF} = 50\ \text{V} \)
  • Junction potentials: \( V_{JE} = V_{JS} = V_{JC} = 0.6\ \text{V} \)
  • Supply voltages: \( V_{DD}, V_{CC} = \pm 15\ \text{V} \)

I've Simulated Ideal & Calculated μA741.

For Ideal OpAmp \(A_{v} = 108\ dB\)

As you may notice from above calculated plot is not quit linear.

Note

I found that almost all of the hand-analysis and simulated results matched, except for \( I_{C14} \). The hand analysis gave \( I_{C14} = 138\ \mu\text{A} \), while the simulation gave approximately \( 52\ \mu\text{A} \). I have not yet figured out why the difference is so large.

items.title: 1. Subgroup Metrics & Definitions
items.text:
For a process monitored across \( k \) subgroups, where each subgroup contains \( n \) observations:

  • Subgroup Sample Size: \( n \)
  • Subgroup Count: \( k \)

items.title: 2. X-bar (\( \bar{X} \)) Chart
items.text: Monitors the central tendency of the process over time.

items.title: Subgroup Mean
items.text: \[ \bar{X}_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} X_{ij}}{n} \]

items.title: Grand Mean (Center Line)
items.text: \[ \bar{\bar{X}} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} \bar{X}_j}{k} \]

items.title: Control Limits Using Range (\( \bar{R} \))
items.text: \[ UCL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} + A_2 \bar{R} \] \[ CL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} \] \[ LCL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} - A_2 \bar{R} \]

items.title: Control Limits Using Standard Deviation (\( \bar{S} \))
items.text:
\[ UCL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} + A_3 \bar{S} \] \[ CL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} \] \[ LCL_{\bar{X}} = \bar{\bar{X}} - A_3 \bar{S} \]

plot 🕐

items.title: 3. Range (R) Chart
items.text: Monitors within-subgroup variation for small sample sizes (typically \( n \le 8 \) or \( 10 \)).

items.title: Subgroup Range
items.text: \[ R_j = X_{\max, j} - X_{\min, j} \]

items.title: Average Range (Center Line)
items.text: \[ \bar{R} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} R_j}{k} \]

items.title: Control Limits
items.text:
\[ UCL_R = D_4 \bar{R} \] \[ CL_R = \bar{R} \] \[ LCL_R = D_3 \bar{R} \]

plot 🕑

items.title: 4. Standard Deviation (S) Chart
items.text: Monitors process variation for moderate-to-large sample sizes (\( n > 8 \) or \( 10 \)) or variable subgroup sizes.

items.title: Average Standard Deviation (Center Line)
items.text: \[ \bar{S} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} S_j}{k} \]

items.title: Control Limits
items.text:
\[ UCL_S = B_4 \bar{S} \] \[ CL_S = \bar{S} \] \[ LCL_S = B_3 \bar{S} \]

plot 🕒

items.title: 5. Within-Subgroup Sigma Estimates
items.text:
To estimate the short-term process standard deviation (\( \hat{\sigma} \)) for capability analysis:

From Range:

\[ \hat{\sigma}_R = \frac{\bar{R}}{d_2} \]

From Standard Deviation:

\[ \hat{\sigma}_S = \frac{\bar{S}}{c_4} \]

Note

The constants \( A_2, A_3, D_3, D_4, B_3, B_4, d_2, \) and \( c_4 \) are unbiasing control chart factors that depend only on the subgroup sample size \( n \).
